  "$RUNNER_NAME" "$disk" "$memory"
# Node governance level from the node's one status file; never fails the probe.
python3 -I -B - /mnt/c/ProgramData/Clued/node-governance/status.json <<'PY' ||
import json, sys
level, written = "unknown", None
try:
    with open(sys.argv[1], encoding="utf-8-sig") as handle:
        row = json.load(handle)
    if row.get("level") in ("green", "yellow", "red"):
        level = row["level"]
    if isinstance(row.get("writtenAt"), str):
        written = row["writtenAt"][:64]
except Exception:
    pass
print("COMPUTE_PANEL_GOVERNANCE " + json.dumps({"level": level, "writtenAt": written}, separators=(",", ":")))
PY

source_yaml_lines: # Compute panel (Task 679a0c2b, Owner Decision 183ee67c): every five minutes
# each general-pool runner answers a route probe (its name, free disk,
# available memory and node governance level), and one Linux runner rebuilds the panel issue from those
# probes, the in-progress jobs of every workflow, the resident executors'
# info-only PR statuses and, for the duplicate-run alert (Task e435e658), the
# check runs of recent PR heads (checks: read). It uses only this workflow's
# GITHUB_TOKEN; no secret reaches the pool. See scripts/ci/self-hosted/compute_panel.py and
# stay on hosted runners: the pool cannot watch its own complete loss.
# A run by hand: GitHub may delay or skip */5 schedules (none ran in the first hour after #935).
# A new run cancels the previous one, so an offline runner holds at most one
# queued probe. Probes that already finished keep their result.
# Work Claim Admission v0.1 §4.6 L0b: the heavy jobs below run only when
# Clued admits this pull request. The gate does not call Clued and gets no
# Clued token (this job runs PR code): it waits for the trusted
# pull_request_target run of clued-work-admission.yml on this head and reads
# its result, always enforced (Merge Admission step 6 retired the advisory
# switch CLUED_WORK_ADMISSION_ENFORCE); non-PR events are admitted.
# Self-hosted Linux pool, pinned Node (Decision f86179b3).
runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal]
# One probe per runner, each on its own literal route. The job name is what
# compute_panel.py reads; it prints one COMPUTE_PANEL_PROBE line.
runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal, runner-company-linux-01]
# Node governance level from the node's one status file; never fails the probe.
runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal, runner-company-linux-02]
# Node governance level from the node's one status file; never fails the probe.
runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal, runner-company-linux-03]
# Node governance level from the node's one status file; never fails the probe.
runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal, runner-company-linux-04]
# Node governance level from the node's one status file; never fails the probe.
# The two general Windows runners are told apart by their site label.
runs-on: [self-hosted, Windows, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal, cap-python312, site-company]
# Node governance level from the node's one status file; never fails the probe.
runs-on: [self-hosted, Windows, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal, cap-python312, site-home]
# Node governance level from the node's one status file; never fails the probe.
runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal]
# -I: the runner is shared, so ignore user site-packages and PYTHON* settings.

source_yaml_lines: # The merge train's front brought up to date with main (Owner Decisions
# scripts/ci/clued-front-main-merge.mjs). The on-duty node's companion starts
# it when stage 10 says FRONT_NEEDS_MAIN_MERGE (front-merge-dispatch.mjs), with
# the PR and the head the train named; a person may start it the same way.
# As the clued-admission App it does one thing, only when it is still true:
# update-branch of that PR from that head (GitHub merges main in itself and
# refuses a conflict or a moved head), then the App's check kooyumi-main-merge
# on the new merge commit, by which the admission keeps the holder's head
# authorization (migration 20261116090000). It holds no Clued credential.
# Only workflow_dispatch: this file and the script run from the default
# branch, with the clued-admission environment's App key (deployment branches
# limited to main); the inputs are only a request, every fact is read again.
description: Pull request number of the train front
description: Its head SHA as the train saw it
runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal]
# Owner Decision 22b0e0ed: admit on the independent CI's own App 5368905 kooyumi-work-admission
# check for this exact head, polled for at most 10 minutes; never on another App's check.
# The self-hosted pool, as clued-native617-admission-dispatch.yml with the same environment (new hosted execution is prohibited).
runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal]
# One at a time; a second request for the same front reads the state the first one left.
- name: Bring main into the train front

source_yaml_lines: # Work Claim Admission v0.1 §4.6, hand dispatch (Owner Decision 75abfe80,
# Task 29128827). Agents act through the Owner's account, so a heavy workflow
# dispatched by hand must first have its claim verified here:
#   1. Dispatch this workflow on the default branch with the heavy workflow,
#      the ref it will run on and the claim id. This run verifies the claim
#   2. Dispatch the heavy workflow on that ref with admission_run_id = this
#      run's id. Its admission-gate admits only when this run succeeded on the
#      default branch within 30 minutes and names that workflow and ref.
# The Clued token comes from the `clued-admission` environment, whose
# deployment branches are limited to main; the job also refuses any other ref.
# Default-branch code only; the dedicated runner stays disabled pending qualification.
description: Existing exact workflow/ref dispatch admission
description: Heavy workflow that will be dispatched
description: Branch or tag the heavy workflow will run on
description: Live Clued work claim covering this run
description: Claim scope, global or project:<canonical_project_id>
runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, clued, pool-general, trust-internal]
runs-on: [self-hosted, Linux, X64, clued, trust-internal, handover-native-control-once]
# Re-review 4, m6: the default branch as it is now, so a re-run of an
# old run does not replay that run's older code with today's secrets.
- name: Refuse until independent Native E1 qualification
- name: Verify the work claim with Clued
- name: Export the closed local natural R9 packet
- name: Preserve natural R9 source observations
